Subject: Request: Embeddings pricing — per-vector vs per-token + dimension mapping

Hi Kimberly,

We're evaluating Redwood for a large semantic search rollout and need a clear baseline on how you price embeddings so we can model costs. Specific asks:

- Baseline hosted rates (per-vector) for typical dimensions (1536, 3072, 8192). If you also have a per-token equivalent for long-document chunking that would help.
- Which Redwood-verified embedding models map to which dimensions (model name -> dims).
- Do you bill per-vector produced, or per-token for the input when we pass long documents? How do you count vectors for batched requests / multi-chunking?
- Any quantization or compression options that change pricing? If so, what are the performance tradeoffs?
- Volume tiers / commit discount examples (we expect an initial pilot of ~200k vectors/month, then scale to 3–5M/month in year 1).

Attached is a tiny sample CSV of documents (searchlytics-example-batch.csv) so you can sanity-check the cost math. Can you send a simple one-page rate card PDF and a short worked example for our pilot vs full-scale?

Would like to share the numbers with finance this week — can you aim to get something over by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks —
Ava

Searchlytics

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request: Embeddings pricing — per-vector vs per-token + dimension mapping

Hi Ava — thanks for the clear brief and the sample CSV. Quick summary and an attached one-pager (redwood-embed-ratecard-2027.pdf) to share with finance. High-level answers below, then a couple of clarifying questions so we can give the tightest pricing.

1) Baseline hosted per-vector rates (public list; enterprise commits vary):
   - text-embed-3-small (1536d): $0.00035 per vector
   - text-embed-3-large (3072d): $0.00062 per vector
   - text-embed-3-xl (8192d): $0.00145 per vector

2) Token vs vector billing: we charge per-vector for embeddings API calls. If you submit long documents that we chunk and embed, you are billed per vector produced (i.e., number of chunks). For customers that ingest raw text and prefer pricing tied to input tokens, we can provide a per-1k-token equivalence for modeling — but actual invoiceable unit is per vector. Example: for text-embed-3-small we assume avg chunk size ~1.5k tokens -> ~1 vector per 1.5k tokens for long documents (this is model- and tokenizer-dependent).

3) Batched requests: billing is per output vector. A single batched request that returns N vectors counts as N billable vectors. Parallelism or batching does not change unit count, only latency/cost efficiency on your side.

4) Quantization/compression: we support server-side 8-bit quantized execution for storage/serving; that reduces compute cost but not the billed vector count. For customers who opt for aggressive on-disk compression (e.g., 4-bit PQ) we can provide a reduced storage fee and an optional lower per-vector operational rate (custom pricing).

5) Volume tiers (public):
   - 0–500k vectors/mo: list rates above
   - 500k–2M: -8% off list
   - 2M–10M: -15% off list
   - >10M: contact sales for bespoke pricing

Sample worked example (pilot -> steady state):
   - Pilot (200k vectors/mo) on text-embed-3-large: 200,000 * $0.00062 = $124/mo (list)
   - Steady (4M vectors/mo) after 15% tier: 4,000,000 * ($0.00062 * 0.85) ≈ $2,108/mo

Clarifying Qs so we can tighten a proposal:
 - Typical document length (avg tokens) and whether you dedupe / pre-filter before embedding
 - Target latency SLOs (do you need dedicated capacity / SLA?)
 - Which vector store(s) you plan to use (we commonly see Pinecone, Milvus, FAISS).

Next steps: attached rate card PDF plus a short spreadsheet I'll send after you confirm the deployment pattern. If you'd like, we can do a technical call tomorrow to validate chunking assumptions and run a small pilot for accurate billing estimates.

Best,
Kimberly Park

Hi Ava — looping in Ben from sales engineering. A few quick answers to your follow-ups, and a proposed next step (pilot + commercial sketch).

1) Migration between dims: yes, migrating from 1536 -> 3072 requires re-embedding (new vectors are new billable outputs). We do a staged roll where you can backfill with a service window to spread the cost; during a migration we can offer a migration credit to offset re-ingest costs (typical: 12% credit on the re-ingest charge for migrations >1M vectors).

2) Quantization compatibility: compressed vectors (PQ/4-bit) are compatible with most ANN indexes but you get tradeoffs in recall. We can provide a small evaluation (100k vectors) to measure recall delta across HNSW/IVF in your workload. Storage example: 4-bit PQ reduces on-disk size by ~4–8x depending on config; compute reduction on serving depends on whether you use a quantized local runtime or CPU fallback.

3) Dedup / caching: we do not de-duplicate at billing time based on vector equality. Billing is per vector produced by the embeddings API. That said, if you use our prefix / KV caching layer at inference time to avoid re-embedding identical inputs, you will reduce billable vectors. The caching layer is controllable and we can help configure TTLs for batch-ingest workflows.

Commercial sketch for 3M vectors/mo commitment (example term sheet):
 - Commitment: 3,000,000 vectors/mo, 12 months
 - Effective price: list rates with 15% committed discount across all dims
 - Ramp / true-up: quarterly reconciliation; overages billed at committed price + 10% premium; under-usage credited pro-rata each quarter
 - Migration credit: as above for first re-ingest during migration window
 - SLA: 99.9% availability for hosted inference endpoints; credits detailed in SOW for Dedicated or Private deployments

If this aligns, we can draft a short mutual action plan and a pilot SOW (30–90 days, up to 250k vectors) that validates chunking, latency and cost. Proposed next step: 30m call tomorrow 2pm PST?

Best,
